features.name: ASA object NAT/PAT
features.refusal_reason: PT's ASA 9.6 image rejects every NAT form tested (object NAT, twice NAT, classic nat/global) with CLI status 2, so no translation can be configured. Use a router for NAT (S3.A6) or terminate outside PT.

features.name: ASA DHCP server
features.evidence: probes/raw/S3.asa-lab.txt (inside PC leased 10.99.0.100 from the ASA)

features.name: ASA object groups
features.refusal_reason: PT's ASA 9.6 image rejects `object-group network` and any ACL that references a group with CLI status 2. Use a plain address-scoped ACL (S3.C1).

features.name: Server-PT services API probe
features.evidence: probes/raw/S3.processes.txt (DnsServer, HttpServer, DhcpServerMain, EmailServer, FtpServer, NtpServer, SyslogServer and AcsServer are exposed)

features.name: App-level DNS/HTTP proof
features.evidence: probes/raw/S3.dns-http.txt (nslookup/ping server.local and an HTTP body returned)

features.name: HTTP/HTTPS service
features.evidence: probes/raw/S3.dns-http.txt (PC fetched the configured index.html body over HTTP; the HTTPS path was not separately exercised)

features.name: Email service
features.refusal_reason: The EmailServer configuration call (`updateAllAccounts`) blocks the Script Engine and closes Packet Tracer, so no mail flow can be driven. Use an external mail server.

features.name: FTP service
features.evidence: probes/raw/S3.ftp-login.txt (PC console `ftp 10.89.0.2` -> `230- Logged in`, `ftp>` prompt, `221- Service closing` on quit; the server's FTP process is read back enabled with the user account)

features.name: AAA (RADIUS/TACACS) server
features.refusal_reason: The ACS server accepts the user and client records and the router accepts the radius-server and tacacs-server configuration, but an SSH login against either path times out; PT does not complete the AAA exchange. Use local AAA (S3.A15) or an external AAA server.

features.name: NTP/Syslog server
features.evidence: probes/raw/S3.ntp-syslog.txt (NTP server configured and read back; five syslog entries from the router arrived)

features.name: Custom SSID / WPA2
features.refusal_reason: The AP accepts and reads back a custom SSID/WPA2, but every documented client profile call (addProfile, setCurrentProfile, setCurrentProfileStringIPs) is rejected by this PT build and no antenna link forms. Use the default SSID (S3.E1/S3.E3).

features.name: Smartphone/tablet wireless clients
features.evidence: probes/raw/S3.e3-clients.txt (both associated, DHCP .2/.3, flows both ways)

features.name: WLC + lightweight APs
features.refusal_reason: PT has no placeable lightweight AP model (LAP-PT/3702i are rejected) and WLC-PT exposes only a base CapwapAC process, so a WLC join cannot be built. Use autonomous APs.

features.name: Multiple SSIDs to VLANs
features.refusal_reason: The AP's WirelessServer has one SSID and no SSID-to-VLAN mapping method; PT offers no multi-SSID/VLAN API. Use separate APs/VLANs or the default SSID.

features.name: Explicit cloud mapping driver
features.evidence: probes/raw/S3.cloud-lab.txt (two Frame Relay circuits on one cloud; customer A/B isolation blocked)

features.name: Cloud serial / Frame Relay
features.evidence: probes/raw/S3.cloud-lab.txt (DLCI 100<->200 Frame Relay through the cloud; ping reachable)

features.name: IoT registration API probe
features.evidence: probes/raw/S3.iot-api.txt (Smart-LED IoeClient exposes setupRemoteApi/reportStates; no IoT server process on the HomeRouter)

features.name: IoT registration + control
features.refusal_reason: The Smart-LED exposes IoeClient, but the HomeRouter has no IoeServer and no registration/control path is exposed, so a registered on/off control cannot be driven. Configure the IoT service in the PT GUI.

features.name: Printer/IP phone/tablet/smartphone endpoints
features.refusal_reason: Printer-PT, tablet and smartphone are proven endpoints, but the 7960's Vlan1 never comes up (no usable CLI, isPortUp false with the wall port linked and powered), so the IP phone cannot be a flow endpoint. Use a PC/laptop as the voice endpoint or a downstream PC behind the phone.
